title: Ensembl's history carries a gene to another place
what: an id (or the gene a symbol named at its release) is followed through Ensembl's history to a gene that shares no or less of the old gene model's exon bases than another gene at the old place: idtrack answers Ensembl's successor, the reads a count matrix gave the old feature lie mostly in another gene of the target release
user_action: read the place of the answer (explain); to merge count matrices, map features by place where the source release shares the target's assembly (rosetta's step 4) or through the chain file
fixed_by: rule `place_moves_marked` (idtrack's next version: a move of place marked in the result); the disagreement is Ensembl's

title: Ensembl's history carries a gene to another place
what: the old model's place holds no one gene of the target release, and Ensembl's history leads to a gene outside that place

title: Ensembl's history carries a gene to another place
what: a symbol read as the gene Ensembl's GTF names so at the source release, followed by Ensembl's history to a gene away from that gene's place

title: a split whose old place holds one successor
what: Ensembl split the gene; the old model's place holds one of the successors: `all` returns every successor, `best` may tie
user_action: use `best`, or keep the successor that overlaps the old place (explain gives each candidate's path)

title: `best` chooses a successor of a split away from the old place
what: among the successors of a split, `best` answers one that the old model's place does not hold
fixed_by: none decided (an open question: rank the successors of a split by the old place)

title: Ensembl gave a gene a new id without an event
what: Ensembl retires the id without successor while a gene of the target release lies at the same place (a re-annotation: pig 101 -> 115, mouse GRCm38 -> GRCm39): idtrack answers nothing (no bridge)
user_action: map by place (rosetta's step 4; the chain file across assemblies); `allow_bridges` where a bridge reaches the same place
fixed_by: rule `bridge_same_place` (idtrack's next version) for bridges; the missing events are Ensembl's

title: Ensembl gave a gene a new id without an event
what: a symbol read as the gene Ensembl's GTF names so; Ensembl retires that gene without successor while a gene of the target release lies at its place

title: a successor in Ensembl's history, no answer
what: Ensembl's history (strict walk) has a successor; idtrack answers nothing

title: a successor in Ensembl's history, no answer
what: a symbol read at its release as the GTF's gene, whose history has a successor; idtrack answers nothing

title: a display name of the source release is not found
what: Ensembl's GTF names a gene so at the source release; idtrack does not find the string there (miRBase names, names the graph's name databases lack)
user_action: ask by Ensembl id, or another name database
fixed_by: idtrack's next version/decided: rule `mirbase_genes` for miRBase

title: names from other name sources
what: the answer adds genes that carry the string in another name source (UniProt gene name, NCBI label) or as a synonym at the source release, not as Ensembl's display name

title: a symbol answered with a gene it does not name in the source release's GTF
what: idtrack reads the string as another gene's name in another source, as a synonym, or at another release, while Ensembl's GTF of the source release gives it to another gene

title: wrong answers without a cause, read one by one
what: answers no test of the classifier explains (docs/families/d.md, "Causes")

title: a name of several genes: `all` misses some of them
what: several genes carry the string as their Ensembl name at the source release; idtrack's graph gives it to only some of them (miRBase names are not in the graph), so `all` returns only their successors

title: the answer carries the string in a database the truth does not read (not idtrack's)
what: the returned gene carries the string in Vega gene, Havana gene or VGNC at the release read; D1's truth reads Ensembl's display names only

title: without `from_release`, a symbol is read at another release than Ensembl's display names say
what: rule `start_release` reads an identifier at the target release where it is active there, else at the latest release where it is active; idtrack counts every name database, the truth Ensembl's display name only

title: names from other name sources
what: the answer adds genes that carry the marker string in another name source (UniProt gene name, NCBI label) or as a synonym

title: a name of several genes: `all` misses some of them
what: as for D1

title: a marker that Ensembl names a gene at the list's release is not found
user_action: ask by Ensembl id, or with another name database

title: missing-value strings answered instead of refused (d4c2dda)
what: `nan`, `NA`, `None`, `null` in a list are looked up as identifiers and answered nothing on d4c2dda; rule `missing_values` (71690ab) raises MissingValueError for each

title: miRBase names not in the graph
what: miRNA genes whose display name is a miRBase name are not found by that name or its separator forms
user_action: use the Ensembl id or the HGNC/MGI symbol of the miRNA gene

title: `infer_source` cannot tell the release of a list of symbols
what: every string is read as what it means at the graph's last release and counted in every name database, so a list of names is inferred at the newest releases where its names still exist (rosetta's matrices: 115), or with the neighbouring releases where they live in another source tied (synthetic lists of display names), whatever release its table was made from
user_action: infer the release from the table's Ensembl ids, or by reading the names at every release (rosetta's tiers)

title: a separator variant read as another gene's synonym
what: idtrack's separator search finds the spelling as a synonym of other genes at an older release, where the name's own gene carries it only as written otherwise
user_action: type the name as the authority writes it
